spec_results.name: integrator_ugbw_gt_fclk
spec_results.comparison: worst-corner UGBW >= fclk (so OTA settles within T/2 @ 1 MHz)
spec_results.note: worst-corner UGBW=1.81 MHz across all 9 PVT corners; all 9 corners have real ngspice UGBW > 1 MHz

spec_results.name: ota_dc_gain_informational
spec_results.note: nominal (tt/27C) OTA open-loop gain=66.56727 dB. Open-loop test harness has no CMFB -> DC bias (and thus gain at bias) varies by corner (range 23.5..66.6 dB). Informational: a closed-loop SC integrator self-biases via the feedback cap; settling is governed by UGBW (the PASS spec above).

sc_integrator_step_settling.result: vout 0.960 V -> 0.874 V after a +100 mV input step, monotonic, no ringing -> stable, settles well within T/2=500 ns @ 1 MHz

comparator_1bit_decision.result: clocked latch resolves input sign in BOTH polarities (win1 vinp>vinn -> oa-ob<0; win2 inputs flipped -> oa-ob>0)

ota_open_loop.result: nominal DC gain 66.6 dB, UGBW 14.9 MHz (tt/27C)

unverified_metrics.name: ENOB
unverified_metrics.reason: End-to-end ENOB/SNDR requires a full OSR-256 incremental conversion window (>= 256 clocks) of the closed ΔΣ loop + the digital decimation filter + an output FFT. That is a mixed-signal (analog modulator + digital decimator) cosim, not a single analog SPICE transient. The analog primitives it depends on (OTA gain/BW, integrator settling, 1-bit quantizer) ARE verified above; the system-level ENOB is deferred to mixed-signal cosim (track M1-M4 / A9, WAIVED per L9 — no silicon).

unverified_metrics.name: SNDR
unverified_metrics.reason: Same as ENOB — needs the full conversion-window FFT.

note: Real ngspice-45.2 on sky130A transistor-level decks. PVT = ss/tt/ff x -40/27/125 C. Per L9: IHP SG13G2 has no public ngspice corner lib, so sky130 device models are the documented standin (modeled, NOT silicon sign-off). ENOB/SNDR are system-level and remain unverified here (see unverified_metrics).
